question: Why did Camden Council refuse to provide the annual spending figures on hair strand testing in family court proceedings, and what case management system limitation contributed to this refusal?
expected_answer: Camden Council refused the request under Section 12 of the Freedom of Information Act because the cost of compliance would exceed the appropriate limit of £450 (equivalent to 18 hours at £25 per hour). The information is not held in a reportable format because there is no routine way of recording cases in proceedings within the Children's Services case management system, MOSAIC, meaning identifying the relevant data would require a manual review.

question: Which companies were responsible for scaffolding and play equipment on the Agar Grove 1C project?
expected_answer: Scaffolding was carried out by BMS Scaffolding Ltd, and play equipment was supplied by Wicksteed Playgrounds.

question: How many Return Home Interviews were completed by Camden Council in the period 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025, and in how many of those was 'Family Conflict' identified as a risk factor?
expected_answer: 464 Return Home Interviews were completed in the period 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025, and 'Family Conflict' (the closest equivalent to 'parental conflict') was identified in 40 of those interviews.

question: If I am unhappy with Camden Council's response to my FOI request about City of Sanctuary funding, what steps can I take and who should I contact at each stage?
expected_answer: First, you can request an Internal Review within 2 months by emailing foireviews@camden.gov.uk or writing to Information and Records Management Team, London Borough of Camden, Town Hall, Judd Street, London WC1H 9JE, quoting your case reference number. If unsatisfied with the Internal Review outcome, you can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) at casework@ico.org.uk, by telephone on 0303 123 1113, via live chat at https://ico.org.uk/global/contact-us/live-chat/, or through their webform. Note that Camden Council does not consent to its contact details being used for marketing purposes.

question: Why did Camden Council refuse to provide information about the removal or conversion of resident parking spaces in the CA-C zone, and how did they justify this decision in terms of public interest?
expected_answer: Camden Council refused the request under EIR 2004 regulation 12(4)(b) (manifestly unreasonable) because processing it would be disproportionately burdensome. They estimated they would need to review approximately 200 decision reports since January 2021, taking a minimum of 15 minutes per report, plus additional time for redaction. On the public interest balance, while they acknowledged releasing the information would improve transparency, they concluded the arguments for withholding outweighed disclosure because: processing would place a large burden on officer time and cost (High), it would divert resources from core business activities (High), it would detrimentally impact services to the public (High), and it is not in the public interest for the Council to neglect public services for one information request (High).

question: What information is Camden Council asked to provide regarding refugee resettlement schemes and empty residential properties in this FOI request?
expected_answer: Regarding refugee resettlement schemes (questions 6-9), Camden is asked to provide: the total number of individuals and households allocated housing under any refugee resettlement, asylum dispersal, or humanitarian protection scheme since 2015 (broken down by year and scheme name), the funding sources for each scheme, copies of any agreements or contracts with private developers, housing associations, or investors for properties under those schemes, and explicit confirmation if no such agreements exist. Regarding empty properties (questions 10-12), Camden is asked to provide: the total number of residential properties recorded as empty for each of the past 10 years broken down by classification (short-term vacant, long-term vacant, second homes, uninhabitable premises, etc.), any recorded strategies or action plans to bring empty homes back into use along with supporting evidence on local housing need, and explicit confirmation if no such strategies or data exist.

question: Has Camden Council received any specific advice or guidance about the independence of the Section 151 Officer, and what external reviews have considered the council's financial governance structure?
expected_answer: Camden Council has not specifically received or sought any internal or external advice relating to best practice, CIPFA guidance, audit recommendations, or regulator expectations concerning the seniority, independence, or board-level access of the Section 151 Officer. However, CIPFA has published open guidance on the role of the Chief Financial Officer available on its website. Regarding external reviews, the council's recent peer review included consideration of governance and organisational culture, with findings published publicly. The council's Annual Governance Statement also sets out the governance framework. The current arrangements are noted to be interim, with no long-term decision yet made.

question: If I am unhappy with Camden Council's FOI response, what steps can I take to escalate my complaint, and who are the key contacts at each stage?
expected_answer: First, you can request an Internal Review within 2 months by emailing foireviews@camden.gov.uk or writing to the Information and Records Management Team at London Borough of Camden, Town Hall, Judd Street, London WC1H 9JE, quoting your case reference number. If unsatisfied with the Internal Review outcome, you can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) at casework@ico.org.uk, telephone 0303 123 1113, via live chat at https://ico.org.uk/global/contact-us/live-chat/, or webform at https://ico.org.uk/global/contact-us/. The response was signed by Lorna Jonas-Tinson, Information Rights Officer.

question: I submitted an FOI request to Camden Council about Traffic Management Orders for parking. What specific categories of parking controls were requested, and how has Camden made these traffic orders available to the public?
expected_answer: The specific categories of parking controls requested were: (a) on-street parking places, (b) residents' permit bays, (c) waiting and loading restrictions, (d) shared-use bays, (e) paid-for parking/pay-and-display areas, (f) disabled bays, (g) visitor permit arrangements, and (h) controlled parking zones affecting stationary vehicles. Camden Council has made all traffic orders map-based and publicly available via the Traffic Orders link on their website, where the relevant articles and map tiles can be downloaded as needed.

question: How many vape shop retail applications were approved or rejected in Camden in 2023 and 2024?
expected_answer: Camden Council does not hold this information. There is currently no legislation requiring vape shops to obtain a licence, so the Licensing Team does not hold data on how many vape shops operate within the borough or when they began trading. Therefore, no figures for approved or rejected applications exist for 2023 or 2024.

question: For the FOI request about fly tipping communications at Primrose Gardens, which parts of the request were directed to the Open Data Portal and which parts of the request were refused because the information is not held?
expected_answer: Questions 1, 2, and 3 (regarding communications to residents, investigative action, and enforcement action in 2024 and 2025) were directed to the Open Data Portal at https://opendata.camden.gov.uk/browse, as the information is already reasonably accessible there and is excepted under Regulation 6(1)(b). Question 4, regarding meeting minutes relating to fly tipping, was refused because the council does not hold this information, as officers do not formally minute meetings. This is excepted under Regulation 12(4)(a) of the EIR 2004.

question: How many domiciliary care contracts were handed back to Camden Council by providers in 2024/25 and 2025/26, and what types of providers and care packages does this data cover?
expected_answer: Zero contracts were handed back in both 2024/25 and 2025/26. The data covers both private and third sector providers, and includes any kind of care or support package commissioned by the local authority.

question: What are Camden's mainstream school SEND funding bands and at what threshold are they applied, and did these rates change between 2024-25 and 2025-26?
expected_answer: Camden has two mainstream support bands: Band 1 at £10,857 and Band 2 at £17,418. These top-up rates are applied above £11,000 (rather than the national threshold of £6,000) due to Camden's policy of devolving additional high needs funding to mainstream schools. The rates were introduced in April 2024 and remained unchanged in April 2025, so they are identical for both 2024-25 and 2025-26.

question: How many garages does Camden Council own, and what was the approximate annual income from garage lettings in the most recent completed financial year?
expected_answer: Camden Council owns or manages 2,449 garages (1,445 occupied and 1,005 void). The most recent completed financial year's income was £885,793 in 2024/25 (with 2025/26 being an estimate of £969,301).

question: How many secure residential cycle spaces are there in Camden currently, and how many will there be once the planned installations before May 2026 are complete?
expected_answer: There are currently 2526 spaces across 421 on-street hangars. A further 77 hangars are planned to be installed before May 2026, adding 462 spaces, bringing the total to 2988 spaces.

question: How much did Camden Council pay Multiverse and where did the funding come from, and what data did Camden share with Multiverse as part of the arrangement?
expected_answer: Camden Council paid £7,446 to Multiverse, funded from the apprenticeship levy (not from the council budget). The data shared with Multiverse included the learners' new Camden contact details, Camden's Apprenticeship Service Digital Account ID (to allow payment via the levy), and contact details for the apprentices' managers.

question: How many ex-right to buy properties has Camden Council's buy back team purchased, and where can I find information about a similar recent FOI request with a shorter timeframe?
expected_answer: Camden Council's buy back team has purchased approximately 150 ex-right to buy properties since 2005 (the earliest data they hold), some through the First Refusal process and others from the open market. A similar recent FOI request covering a shorter timeframe was answered and is published on the Council's Open Data Portal under reference CAM11332.

question: What is the difference in cost between a resident and non-resident purchasing both a standard adult burial and the Exclusive Right of Burial in Camden, and how is 'non-resident' defined?
expected_answer: For a standard adult interment, residents pay £1,500 and non-residents pay £2,600 (a difference of £1,100). For the Exclusive Right of Burial, residents pay £1,995 and non-residents pay £4,050 (a difference of £2,055). A non-resident is defined as anyone who lived in any borough other than Islington or Camden at the time of their death or at the point of grave purchase.

question: Who signed the FOI response about the amount owed by North Central London Integrated Care Board to Camden, and how can I request an Internal Review if I'm unhappy with how it was handled?
expected_answer: The response was signed by Lorna Jonas-Tinson, Information Rights Officer. If you are unhappy with how the response was handled, you can request an Internal Review within 2 months by emailing foireviews@camden.gov.uk or writing to the Information and Records Management Team, London Borough of Camden, Town Hall, Judd Street, London WC1H 9JE, quoting your case reference number.

question: What business grants does Camden Council currently offer to small and medium sized businesses, and what priority areas do these grants cover?
expected_answer: Camden Council operates three funds: the Future Camden Fund (offering match trading grants of up to £50,000 that match business trading income growth), the Camden Climate Fund (funding for energy efficiency improvements, sustainable transport and other sustainability initiatives, which is sector agnostic), and We Make Camden Kit (delivered in partnership with Camden Giving, open to social enterprises). The Future Camden Fund awards grants by programme priority areas including: programmes for young people, access to STEAM, underrepresentation, citizen health and wellbeing, training and education, digital inclusion, local business support, sustainability, net zero and ethical choices.

question: Where can I find Camden's Authority Monitoring Reports that contain housing land supply information, and what are the most recent reports available?
expected_answer: Camden's Authority Monitoring Reports are publicly available on two platforms: the Camden open data portal at opendata.camden.gov.uk (which includes the 2018-19 report) and data.gov.uk (which includes the 2021-22 and 2022-23 report). The most recent reports available cover the period 2021-22 and 2022-23.

expected_answer: You can request an Internal Review within 2 months by emailing foireviews@camden.gov.uk or writing to the Information and Records Management Team at London Borough of Camden, Town Hall, Judd Street, London WC1H 9JE. If still unsatisfied, you can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) at icocasework@ico.org.uk or by calling 0303 123 1113. The response was signed by Peter Williams, Information Rights Officer.

question: I'm trying to access Camden Council's spend over £500 data for August 2025. When will this be available, and where can I find it?
expected_answer: Camden Council does not yet hold the August 2025 spend data. They are up to date until the end of July 2025, and the August figures will only be available after they have run the relevant reports, which will most likely occur in the 2nd week of September 2025. In the meantime, you can check Open Data Camden portal before making a new request, as your question may already be answered by a previous FOI response or in one of their datasets.

question: What was Camden Council's response to the FOI request about the Youth Guarantee Trailblazer programme, and what should I do if I'm unhappy with how my request was handled?
expected_answer: Camden Council stated that it does not hold the information requested across all three questions about the Youth Guarantee Trailblazer programme (the list of required documents, the main plan/business case, and the performance measures/KPIs). If you are unhappy with how the response was handled, you can request an Internal Review within 2 months by emailing foireviews@camden.gov.uk or writing to the Information and Records Management Team at Town Hall, Judd Street, London WC1H 9JE, quoting your case reference number. If still unsatisfied, you can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office.

question: Does Camden Council have an exemption policy for Blue Badge holders in LTNs, and have there been any complaints about LTN accessibility exemptions or accessibility issues resulting from LTNs?
expected_answer: Camden does not have an exemption policy for Blue Badge holders for at all times motor vehicle restrictions. As a result, they do not hold information on refused permit applications or complaints related to LTN accessibility exemptions. Additionally, there are no complaint cases related to accessibility issues resulting from the implementation of Low Traffic Neighbourhoods (LTNs).
